claim.statement: On 1 May 2026, Persian water-sector reporting moved Tehran's water crisis from simple overnight pressure reduction into an open-ended pressure-management regime: SNN/Vista quoted Isa Bozorgzadeh saying pressure management is already underway, may be reduced further, and will continue until water conditions recover; DidbanIran/Vista quoted Tehran Water and Wastewater management saying Tehran dams were 9% full including Taleghan and 3% without Taleghan, while national dam filling averaged 32%.
claim.subject: Tehran water supply
claim.object: open-ended pressure management under extremely low reservoir fill

evidence.summary: SNN/Vista quotes Isa Bozorgzadeh saying water-pressure management is already underway, may be reduced further, and will continue until water conditions recover.

DidbanIran/Vista quotes Tehran Water and Wastewater management saying national dam filling averages 32%, Tehran dams are 9% full with Taleghan and 3% without Taleghan, and Tehran is passing through hard/bad supply conditions.
Existing KNB source records the earlier official line that Tehran pressure is reduced from around midnight until morning to reduce leakage and refill urban reservoirs.

information_depth.rationale: Two fresh domestic sources and one existing official-spokesman row align on pressure management and very low Tehran reservoir fill.

assessment.uncertainty: The sources establish pressure-management policy and reservoir severity, not exact neighborhood-level outage duration.

claim.statement: Between 30 April and 1 May 2026, severe reservoir stress was visible outside Tehran as well: Shahrara/Vista quoted a water-sector information-policy council member saying Mashhad's four drinking-water dams were only 6% full and 94% empty, with no current rationing plan, while Jahan-Sanat/Vista quoted Karaj water management saying Karaj Dam storage had reached 7%, inflow was below outflow, stored water was being consumed, and current conditions implied roughly 15 days of water absent effective rainfall.
claim.subject: urban drinking-water reservoirs in Mashhad and Karaj
claim.object: severe low-storage conditions without admitted formal rationing

evidence.summary: Shahrara/Vista says Mashhad's Dousti, Torogh, Kardeh, and Ardak drinking-water dams have 6% water and are 94% empty, while authorities say there is currently no water-rationing plan.
Jahan-Sanat/Vista quotes Karaj water management saying Karaj Dam storage is 7%, inflow is below outflow, stored water is being consumed, and about 15 days of water remain under current conditions.

information_depth.rationale: The two city signals are specific and sourced, but not enough to quantify household cutoffs or all affected neighborhoods.

claim.statement: As of 29 April-2 May 2026, electricity stress looked more deferred than water stress: Mehr/Vista quoted the electricity-industry spokesman saying he could not promise no blackouts but expected fewer limits this year; existing KNB rows still show full industrial power only until 20 Ordibehesht / 10 May, post-May-10 weekly allocation risk, transit-fee/debt cutoff risk for production units, and Ettelaat-linked warnings about employment and national security; a 109-item xPool latest sample found no clean coordinated household or industrial blackout complaint cluster, with most 'خاموشی' hits about the internet blackout.
claim.subject: Iranian electricity supply risk
claim.object: a deferred industrial-policy cliff rather than a confirmed current outage mobilization

evidence.summary: Mehr/Vista quotes the electricity-industry spokesman saying he cannot say there will be no blackouts, but limits will be lower this year.
Existing KNB source records official assurance that industries have full electricity until 20 Ordibehesht / 10 May.
Existing KNB source records the production-unit electricity cutoff risk linked to transit fees/debt.
Existing KNB source records Ettelaat-linked warnings that cutting industrial electricity threatens employment and national security.

xPool latest sample emitted 109 items and showed scattered water/electricity comments but no clean coordinated household or industrial blackout complaint cluster; most 'خاموشی' hits were internet-blackout discourse.

information_depth.rationale: Official and prior KNB sources clearly establish the policy cliff; the xPool absence of a complaint cluster is weak negative evidence.

assessment.uncertainty: The conclusion can change quickly after 20 Ordibehesht / 10 May or with local outage footage.

synthesis.title: Cracks in the Islamic Republic, v33 - water is closer to hard rationing than electricity
synthesis.summary: The thirty-third pass shifts back from medicine to basic services. Water has hardened more than electricity. Tehran's overnight pressure reduction is now part of an open-ended pressure-management regime that officials say may deepen and continue until water conditions recover; the same reporting puts Tehran dams at 9% full including Taleghan and 3% without it. This is no longer just a euphemistic cutoff story: Karaj water management is quoted saying Karaj Dam storage is 7% with roughly 15 days of water under current conditions, and Mashhad's four drinking-water dams are reported 94% empty while authorities still deny a rationing plan. Electricity remains dangerous but less immediately visible: officials admit they cannot promise zero blackouts while promising fewer limits, industries are still only guaranteed full power until 20 Ordibehesht / 10 May, and existing rows preserve the debt/transit-fee and employment-risk paths. The xPool pass found scattered water complaints but no coordinated water/electricity protest cluster. Net: water is the live service crack to follow now; electricity's trigger date is still the May 10 industrial decision point.
synthesis.limitations: Reservoir percentages and official pressure-management statements show supply stress and rationing mechanics, not household-level outage duration by neighborhood. The xPool sample is noisy and weak as negative evidence. The next decisive checks are Tehran daytime cutoffs, tanker deployment, Karaj/Mashhad rationing notices, and the 20 Ordibehesht industrial electricity decision.

information_depth.rationale: The synthesis combines direct Persian official/domestic water reporting, existing KNB electricity rows, and a bounded current xPool pass.

operations.rationale: The claim directly updates whether Tehran pressure controls become scheduled or hard household rationing.
Open-ended pressure management is the next step beyond the earlier overnight-pressure-reduction question.
The low Tehran reservoir fill figures and possible further pressure reductions sharpen the Day Zero question.
Karaj and Mashhad reservoir stress show the water crack is not limited to Tehran, though the open question remains framed around Tehran Day Zero.
The claim preserves the 20 Ordibehesht industrial electricity cliff and the hidden debt/transit-fee shutdown path.
The claim weakly tests the household-blackout side of the water/electricity-controls question, while distinguishing internet-blackout chatter from electricity-outage evidence.

operations.reason: v33 updates the active read from medicine budget/insurance rationing to basic-service stress: water pressure management and reservoir depletion now look more immediate than electricity, whose main risk remains the May 10 industrial cliff.
